extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and principal investigators (postdocs, faculty, institutional grants offices)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, experience-based guidance on NIH post-review funding steps (JIT, administrative review, council, NOA, mentor/institution changes) and how to prepare/submit required materials. Focused on navigating administrative/funding decisions after peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Support / JIT disclosure: avoid duplicate funding and show time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH only wants to make sure you are not being funded for the same work twice, and that you have the time to commit to the level of effort documented in your budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List other support (including large company contracts) honestly; non-overlapping projects generally will not hurt funding. Focus on demonstrating no scientific overlap and that you have sufficient effort available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be ready for very fast JIT turnaround
rubrics_metrics.description: When NIH issues a JIT request you will have almost no time to turn it around (as in, a day or two).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have all likely JIT materials prepared in advance (IRB/IACUC, Other Support pages, budget justifications, institutional approvals). If you cannot return JIT quickly, the IC may move to the next application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit regulatory approvals early
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory approvals (IRB, IACUC, clinical trial milestones) may be needed quickly during JIT/administrative review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your project requires regulatory clearances, start those processes early so you can supply approvals within the short JIT window; otherwise funding can be delayed or skipped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Pending Administrative Review'
rubrics_metrics.description: Status can remain 'Pending' for days to months; it simply indicates administrative processing prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays often result from appropriations timing, staff shortages, missing documents, or IC workload. Do not assume a problem if status stays 'Pending'—wait for further contact or status change, and consult your PO/GMS only if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council role: review quality/appropriateness but not fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Council provides a second level of review but does not make funding decisions; they review peer review quality and appropriateness for the IC mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final funding decisions are made by the IC Director after internal funding meetings. Council completion does not equal an award; post-council internal meetings and funding lists follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/SBTT timing may be delayed to later in fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs sometimes postpone SBIR (and other mechanisms) funding decisions until later in the fiscal year to consider all applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t worry immediately if SBIR applications remain pending after Council; schedule and timing vary across ICs and years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized vs automated JIT: respond proactively
rubrics_metrics.description: You may receive only an automated JIT request; ICs don’t always send personalized JIT emails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to the automated JIT portal if possible; have your institutional grants office upload materials and notify your PO/GMS that you complied.

rubrics_metrics.name: ‘Award prepared’ is sufficient to list funding in a new application
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'Award prepared' status is good enough to include the grant in a new application or biosketch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may cite the grant ID (e.g., R01CA123456) and include it in personal statements or research support sections as permitted. Note NIH is transitioning away from Section D research support, but you can still include it until policies change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant start dates can be backdated modestly
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may backdate start dates, but generally not by large amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an award is 'prepared' near a proposed start date, expect the NOA start date to be around the processing date; do not assume extreme retroactive start dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT request is a positive indicator but not a guarantee
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs generally do not request JIT unless they are seriously considering making an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving a JIT is encouraging but not definitive; continue preparing required materials and regulatory approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: PO communications: when and how to contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Officers can advise on funding likelihood and next steps, but PIs should follow institutional policies regarding direct contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure, ask your institutional grants office whether direct contact with the PO is allowed; use the PO to ask whether to resubmit, whether to submit JIT early, or to clarify timelines—but avoid repeated status inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission uncertainty: scores can go up or down
rubrics_metrics.description: A resubmission could result in a better, worse, or similar impact score; there is no policy that an old score is ignored automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss resubmission strategy with your PO. If PO advises resubmission, follow their recommendation and consider asking whether the prior application will still be eligible for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section selection matters for reviewer expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick a study section that matches the priorities and background of reviewers who will appreciate the significance of your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RePORTER Matchmaker and CSR ART tools to find suitable study sections, send a short aims page to the SRO to confirm fit, and consult your PO. Tailor framing (significance vs technical novelty) to the chosen reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: If PO requests a rebuttal before Council, it can be important
rubrics_metrics.description: A PO may ask for a rebuttal to the summary statement to justify further consideration of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a focused rebuttal if requested—this can be a mechanism to clarify concerns and show whether the application should remain under active consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing mentor within same university is administratively simpler
rubrics_metrics.description: If a new mentor is at the same university, you typically do not need an institutional (type 7) change; the PO must approve the mentor change and the institution will submit required documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the new mentor’s biosketch and any requested letters via your sponsored programs office; work with PO and grants office to confirm what else is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing primary mentor or institution for K99/R00 is complex
rubrics_metrics.description: Moving the primary mentor to a different institution (or making the primary mentor remote) is difficult and may not align with what reviewers evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs prefer to stick close to the application reviewed; changing institutions may require a type 7 institutional change and could necessitate reapplication from the new lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare timelines and expect variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Time from submission to award can vary widely (weeks to 16+ months) depending on scores, IC policies, FY appropriations, and administrative processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track status milestones (SRG review, council, pending admin review, award prepared, NOA) and use community timelines as rough guides, but plan for long waits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use institutional grants office for submissions and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions typically handle JIT and formal submissions; some institutions restrict direct PI contact with PO to routed communications through grants offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with your institutional office of sponsored programs/grants management specialist to submit JIT materials and to relay PO communications; ask them to contact NIH when appropriate.
